item.title: Space-filling curves and small-ball probabilities for the Kloosterman process
item.description: arXiv:2610.22645v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct explicitly a space-filling curve in the support of the limiting Kloosterman process, using the planar partial-sum curve of the Rudin--Shapiro sequence. The qualitative existence statement was previously attributed to J. Bober by Kowalski. The resulting curve is a closed, $1/2$-H\"older continuous loop whose image contains a specified triangle of area $1/128$. Its Fourier coefficients are purely imaginary and satisfy $|\widehat f(h)|\leq(2\pi|h|)^{-1}$ for $h\ne 0$. We also prove a uniform lower bound for small balls centred at closed $1/2$-H\"older curves with a fixed coefficient bound, of the form $\exp\{-C\varepsilon^{-2}\log^2(2/\varepsilon)\}$. Known functional convergence then gives a quantitative lower bound for the limiting proportion of two-parameter Kloosterman paths approximating the constructed loop.
item.dc:creator: Danyil Kyselov

item.title: A Non-Split Motohashi Formula for Toric Periods over Number Fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.22728v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a non-split Motohashi formula for toric Eisenstein periods over an arbitrary number field $F$. For a quadratic extension $E/F$, we compare toric Fourier inversion for a product of two Eisenstein series with the $\mathrm{GL}_2/F$-spectral expansion of its Rankin--Selberg kernel. The kernel regularizes the product in a cone of absolute convergence. Eisenstein corrections and contour residues give the geometric and residual terms in the meromorphically continued identity. Suitable test data give twisted first- and second-moment formulas for the completed $L$-functions of everywhere unramified toric characters. Over general $F$ these provide an adelic counterpart of the moment formulas of Duke--Friedlander--Iwaniec that does not use the geometry of Heegner points. In the CM case, we prove the absolute nonvanishing proportion $4.9\times10^{-4}$ for every totally real base field and all sufficiently large CM discriminants, with the threshold depending on the base field and no restriction on the number of ramified primes. We incorporate inverse Euler factors at small ramified primes into the mollifier. Local unit-group tests control the resulting moments and remove the ramified Euler-factor loss.
item.dc:creator: Liyang Yang

item.title: Density Bounds in Hua's Theorem for Prime Squares
item.description: arXiv:2610.22747v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a density version of Hua's theorem in the five-variable case: if $\mathcal P$ is a subset of the primes with relative lower density greater than $0.82$, then every sufficiently large $n\equiv5\pmod{24}$ is a sum of five squares of primes from $\mathcal P$.
item.dc:creator: Michael T. Lacey, Hamed Mousavi, Yaghoub Rahimi, Manasa N. Vempati

item.title: Galois Groups of Trinomials with Small Coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2610.22764v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We calculate the Galois group of $f = x^n + ax^k + b \in \mathbb{Z}\left[ x \right]$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ for all $1 \leq \left| ab \right| \leq 3$, $n$ sufficiently large and $k$ coprime to $n$. In particular, we prove that the Galois group of $f$ is the maximal one that its factorization type allows. We do it by proving a new sufficient condition for the Galois group of a factor of a trinomial to be symmetric, which perhaps can be used to derive stronger results of this kind in the future.
item.dc:creator: Hilel Garmi

item.title: Poisson-Dirichlet statistics for the log-modulus of the Riemann zeta function on expanding intervals near the critical line
item.description: arXiv:2610.22821v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $T > 0$ large, let $\tau$ be uniformly distributed on $[T,2T]$ and let $\sigma = \sigma(T)$ be a deterministic real part approaching $1/2$ from the right. For the Riemann zeta function $\zeta$, we study the Gibbs measure with density proportional to $|\zeta(\sigma + \mathrm{i}\tau + \mathrm{i} h)|^{\beta}$ on $I_{\theta} := [ - (\log{T})^{\theta},(\log{T})^{\theta}]$, for every $\theta > 0$ and $\beta > 0$. As $\beta$ increases, the Gibbs measure increasingly favors positions where $|\zeta|$ is large, providing a way to study the spatial organization of extreme values. Under explicit conditions on the rate at which $\sigma$ approaches the critical line, a phase transition is established at the critical inverse temperature $\beta_{c}(\theta) := 2\sqrt{1 + \theta}$. The limiting distribution of the correlation (or overlap) between the field values at two positions sampled from the Gibbs measure is concentrated at $0$ when $\beta \leq \beta_{c}(\theta)$, and assigns masses $\beta_{c}(\theta)/\beta$ and $1 - \beta_{c}(\theta)/\beta$ to $0$ and $1$, respectively, when $\beta > \beta_{c}(\theta)$. Joint convergence of the overlaps is also established, with the limiting arrays described by Poisson-Dirichlet weights in the low-temperature regime. The Ghirlanda-Guerra identities, which provide recursive relations for the joint overlap distributions, are established in the limit, uniformly for bounded deterministic observables of the sampled positions. All our results are established independently of the Riemann hypothesis.
item.dc:creator: Fr\'ed\'eric Ouimet

item.title: Metric Poissonian Pair Correlation Property Part 2: The Case \(n\log n\)
item.description: arXiv:2610.22833v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that $(\alpha n\log n)_{n\ge1}$ has Poissonian pair correlation for almost every real $\alpha$, solving a Problem posed by Aistleitner, El-Baz and Munsch [Open Problem 3, Geom. Funct. Anal. 2021]. Our main contribution is a new four-point counting estimate with a fixed power saving over $N^{7/3}$ at tolerance $N^{-1}$, valid on the ranges left after a first-moment and Borel--Cantelli argument. Its proof reduces the counting condition to the required proximity of an implicitly defined real root to an integer; a Fej\'er kernel majorizes this condition, and multidimensional van der Corput $A$- and $B$-processes supply the saving. A localized Mellin argument then yields the second-moment estimate needed for the metric conclusion.
item.dc:creator: Bo Tan, Zhen Zhang, Qing-Long Zhou

item.title: Metric Poissonian Pair Correlation Property Part 1: The Case \(n+\log n\)
item.description: arXiv:2610.22836v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that $(\alpha(n+\log n))_{n\ge1}$ has Poissonian pair correlation for Lebesgue almost every real $\alpha$. This solves a Problem posed by Aistleitner, El-Baz and Munsch [Open Problem 2, Geom. Funct. Anal. 2021].
item.dc:creator: Bo Tan, Zhen Zhang, Qing-Long Zhou

item.title: Unconditional Bounds for Two, Three and Four Consecutive Moderate Gaps between Zeros of the Riemann Zeta Function
item.description: arXiv:2610.22927v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove unconditional positive-proportion results for consecutive moderate gaps between zeros of the Riemann zeta function. More precisely, for every fixed \(0<c\leq 1/4\), the lower asymptotic densities, normalized by \(N(T)\), of occurrences of two, three, and four consecutive gaps, each of length at least \(2\pi c/\log T\), are at least \(0.3450014\ldots\), \(0.1812517\ldots\), and \(0.0175021\ldots\), respectively. Here zeros are ordered by ordinate and counted with multiplicity, and \(N(T)\) denotes the number of nontrivial zeros with ordinates in \((0,T]\). This answers unconditionally and quantitatively a question studied by Gonek and Sahay under the Riemann hypothesis and the pair correlation conjecture. In particular, at the time of their work, it was not known unconditionally that even two consecutive moderate gaps occur infinitely often for any fixed \(c>0\). The proof combines Lamzouri's Hilbert-space formulation of the Montgomery--Taylor second-moment method with local spectral estimates for simple critical-line zeros and a cluster-counting argument that accounts for multiple zeros and zeros off the critical line.
item.dc:creator: C\'esar Ang\'on, Erick Ross, Ze Sen Tang, Boyang Zhao

item.title: Improved explicit Burgess-strength bounds for composite moduli
item.description: arXiv:2610.22939v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Consider the character sum $S(M,N)=\sum_{n=M+1}^{M+N}\chi(n)$ for a non-principal Dirichlet character $\chi(n)$ to a (possibly composite) modulus $q$. Burgess proved that $S(M,N)\ll N^{1/2}q^{3/16+\varepsilon}$, for any $\varepsilon>0$. This was made explicit by Jain-Sharma et al., but only for moduli $q\geq \exp(\exp(9.594))\approx 8.03\times 10^{6373}$. We prove a stronger result that holds when $q\geq 1.627\times 10^{19}$.
item.dc:creator: James Punch

item.title: Arithmeticity of critical $L$-values for Hilbert-Siegel modular forms in the left half plane and $s = 1$
item.description: arXiv:2610.23037v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a cuspidal automorphic representation $\pi_f$ generated by a Hilbert-Siegel modular form $f$ and a Hecke character $\mu$ with parallel signature, we show the arithmeticity of critical $L$-values of the standard $L$-function $L^S(s,\pi_f, \mu)$ twisted by $\mu$ in the left half plane. As a consequence, we show the arithmeticity at $s=1$ under the assumption that there exists a nonarchimedean place $v$ such that $\pi_v$ is unramified and $\mu_v$ is ramified.
item.dc:creator: Shuji Horinaga, Hirotaka Kakuhama

item.title: Zagier's 2-3-2 formula for multiple Eisenstein series
item.description: arXiv:2610.23052v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a multiple Eisenstein series analogue of Zagier's formula for the multiple zeta values $\zeta(2,\ldots,2,3,2,\ldots,2)$. The multiple Eisenstein series identity contains correction terms given by derivatives of odd Eisenstein series. Using the Goncharov coproduct and Brown's motivic version of Zagier's formula, we show that the normalized difference has rational Fourier coefficients. We then use the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-structure and a modularity criterion of Yu to prove the identity by induction.
item.dc:creator: Henrik Bachmann

item.title: Minimal asymptotic \(g\)-adic bases from arbitrary partitions
item.description: arXiv:2610.23152v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $g>h\ge2$ be integers. For a nonempty set $W\subseteq\N$, let $\mathcal F^*(W)$ denote the set of its finite nonempty subsets. Let $$A_g(W)=\left\{\sum_{f\in F}a_fg^f: 1\leq a_f \leq g-1,F \in \mathcal F^*(W)\right\},$$ and let $\N=W_1\sqcup\cdots\sqcup W_h$ be a partition into infinite sets. We prove that $A=\bigcup_{i=1}^h A_g(W_i)$ is a minimal asymptotic basis of order $h$ for every such partition.
item.dc:creator: Min Tang

item.title: A $\mathrm{GL}_3$ level analog of Selberg's result for $S(t)$
item.description: arXiv:2610.23201v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\pi$ be a spherical cuspidal $\mathrm{GL}_3$ newform of prime level $N$ and trivial central character, and define $S(t,\pi)=\pi^{-1}\arg L(1/2+\textrm{i}t,\pi)$. Assuming the generalized Riemann hypothesis for $L(s,\pi)$, we establish an asymptotic formula for each fixed weighted moment of $S(t,\pi)$ as $N\to\infty$, for fixed $t>0$. Consequently, under the same weights, $S(t,\pi)/\sqrt{\log\log N}$ converges in distribution to a centered Gaussian distribution of variance $1/(2\pi^2)$. The key input is a weighted orthogonality formula derived from the Kuznetsov formula of prime level.
item.dc:creator: Qingfeng Sun, Hui Wang

item.title: Note on the largest prime factors of consecutive integers
item.dc:creator: Zhiyuan Yang

item.title: Improved $L^p$ maximal estimates for higher-degree Weyl sums
item.description: arXiv:2610.23379v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For each integer $k\ge3$, we establish the following estimate for all $1\le p<\infty$ and $\varepsilon>0$: \[ \left\|\sup_{t\in\mathbb{T}}\left|\sum_{n=1}^N e(nx+n^kt)\right|\right\|_{L^p(\mathbb{T})} \ll_{k,p,\varepsilon} N^{\max\{1-1/K_k,\,1-1/p\}+\varepsilon}, \] where $K_k=\min\{2^{k-1},k(k+1)/2\}$, $e(z)=e^{2\pi iz}$, and $\mathbb{T}=\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$. For $k\ge5$, this improves our earlier bound \cite{chen-miao-yuan-zhao} for $1\le p<D_k$, where $D_k=\min\{2^{k-1},k(k-1)\}$, and, together with the corresponding lower bound, extends the sharp range up to $N^\varepsilon$ from $p\ge D_k$ to $p\ge K_k$. The main new ingredient is a mixed minor-arc moment estimate obtained before taking the time supremum. The minor-arc maximal estimate then follows from a smooth reproducing kernel argument, while the major arcs are handled directly by Poisson summation and classical complete exponential-sum estimates. The reduction from suprema to mean values also yields a short and direct proof of improved $L^p$ estimates for maximal operators on Weyl sums with general polynomial phases, strengthening \cite[Theorem 1.1]{baker-chen-shparlinski}.
item.dc:creator: Xuezhi Chen, Changxing Miao, Jiye Yuan, Tengfei Zhao

item.title: Mahler Method and Vanishing Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.23435v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is motivated by the recent work of Adamczewski and Faverjon [5], who established the algebraic independence of values of Mahler functions satisfying linear functional equations. While their work is a landmark result, some proofs are long and complex. The primary aim of this paper is to simplify those proofs and provide new applications. In their proofs, a vanishing theorem for polynomials, rather than power series, is sufficient. We give a proof of the vanishing theorem without using Szemer\'edi's theorem or Corvaja-Zannier's theorem. In the case of a single transformation, we present a refined vanishing theorem, which allows us to simplify the proof of algebraic independence. We also provide an elementary proof of a vanishing theorem for $q_i$-Mahler functions with various $q_i$. As an application, we prove the algebraic independence of certain continued fractions, extending previous results by Han\v{c}l, Adamczewski, and Bundschuh and V\"a\"an\"anen in which only linear independence and transcendence had been established.
item.dc:creator: Kumiko Nishioka, Taka-aki Tanaka, Yusuke Tanuma

item.title: More than 8/9 zeros of the Riemann zeta function are simple or on the critical line
item.description: arXiv:2610.23467v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove unconditionally that the lower limiting proportion of nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function, which are simple or lie on the critical line, is greater than $8/9$, with zeros counted with multiplicity.
item.dc:creator: Cristian Cobeli, Alexandru Zaharescu

item.title: Lifting mod $p^n$ Galois representations
item.description: arXiv:2610.23579v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We generalize the results of Fakhruddin-Khare-Patrikis, which lift odd mod $p$ Galois representations to geometric $p$-adic representations, to geometric lifting theorems for mod $p^n$ representations whose mod $p$ reduction is odd.
item.dc:creator: Stefan Nikoloski, Stefan Patrikis

item.title: On a series related to the M\"obius function
item.description: arXiv:2610.23660v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a natural number $n>1$ let $P^-(n)$ denote its smallest prime divisor. Alladi and Johnson proved that $\sum_{P^{-}(n)\equiv l \Mod{k}} \frac{\mu(n)\omega(n)}{n} = 0$ for $(l,k)=1$, and Tenenbaum showed that the partial sums of this series up to $X$ are $O_\varepsilon\bigl((\log\log X)^{5/3+\varepsilon}/\log X\bigr)$. In this article, we prove that these partial sums are in fact equal to $C(k,l)/\log X + O\bigl((\log\log X)^4/(\log X)^2\bigr)$, with an explicit constant $C(k,l)$. We also investigate the behaviour of these constants. In particular, we show under GRH that the number of reduced classes $l\Mod{k}$ for which $C(k,l)<0$ is $\varphi(k)(1- o(1))$ as $k\to\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Deep Thakur

item.title: Fourier dimension for exactly approximable matrices
item.description: arXiv:2610.23680v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the Fourier dimension of exactly approximation set for all dimensions. More precisely, let $m,n\ge1$, $\boldsymbol\theta\in\mathbb R^m$, and $\psi:\mathbb N\to \mathbb R^+$ be a non-increasing approximate function. Denote by $\textrm{Exact}_{m,n}(\psi,\boldsymbol\theta)$ the set of $m\times n$ matrices which are inhomogeneously $\psi$-approximable with shift $\boldsymbol\theta$, but not $c\psi$-approximable for any fixed $0<c<1$. We prove that $$\dim_{\text{F}} \textrm{Exact}_{m,n}(\psi,\boldsymbol\theta)=\frac{2n}{1+\tau_\psi},\ \text{whenever }\tau_{\psi}>\frac{n}{m},$$ where $\tau_{\psi}$ is the lower order of $\psi$ at infinity.
item.dc:creator: Yubin He, Bixuan Li, Baowei Wang

item.title: Cuspidal Class Number Formulae for Intermediate Modular Curves of Prime Level
item.description: arXiv:2610.23690v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $X$ be a modular curve lying between $X_{0}(p)$ and $X_{1}(p)$, where $p \ge 13$ is prime. The cuspidal group of $X$ is the subgroup of its Jacobian generated by the equivalence classes of differences of cusps. In this paper, we give explicit formulae for the order of the cuspidal group, and two subgroups of it defined over the rationals.
item.dc:creator: Elvira Lupoian

item.title: Confluence relations, Hoffman basis over \mathbb{Z}_{(2)}, and the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.23719v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We express every admissible word as a $\mathbb{Z}_{(2)}$-linear combination of Hoffman words and explicit confluence relations. This implies that every multiple zeta value is a linear combination of elements of the Hoffman basis with coefficients having odd denominators, as conjectured by Hirose and Sato. Combined with Brown's theorem and Furusho's characterization of the Grothendieck--Teichm\"uller group $\mathrm{GRT}$ by confluence relations, our result identifies the de Rham motivic Galois group of mixed Tate motives over $\mathbb{Z}$ with $\mathrm{GRT}$ and gives an alternative proof of the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture, for which a proof was previously presented in the OpenAI Math Release.
item.dc:creator: Minoru Hirose

item.title: The distribution of $\alpha p$ modulo one in real quadratic function fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.23742v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Matom\"aki proved that if $\alpha\in\R$ is irrational, then there are infinitely many primes $p$ such that $|\alpha-a/p|\le p^{-4/3+\varepsilon}$ for a suitable integer $a$. In \cite{BaMo}, Baier and the author established analogues of this result for $\F_q(T)$ and its imaginary quadratic extensions. In this paper, we extend it to all real quadratic extensions of $\F_q(T)$.
item.dc:creator: Esrafil Ali Molla

item.title: Near optimal gap in the Lonely Runner Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.23790v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a set $V$ of $n$ distinct positive integers, let $\mathrm{ML}(V)=\max_{t\in\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}}\min_{v\in V}\|vt\|$, where $\|x\|$ is the distance from $x$ to the nearest integer. We prove that there is an absolute constant $c>0$ such that for every $n\ge2$ and every $V$, \[ \mathrm{ML}(V)>\frac{1+c}{2n}. \] The proof combines a refinement of the large GCD argument of Green and Walker with a new physical spillover inequality for interval multiplicities.
item.dc:creator: Xiyu Hu, Yifan Jing

item.title: A duality principle for the neighbourhood of manifolds and applications to counting rational points near curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.23797v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish a duality principle relating the count of rationals near a manifold to a sparse counting problem for the dual. As applications, we give a short, self-contained proof of sharp bounds for planar curves under minimal regularity conditions and similarly, sharp upper bounds for non- degenerate space curves, again under minimal curvature conditions. This work recovers and extends the works of Beresnevich, Dickinson and Velani and of Vaughan and Velani on planar curves and independently proves and extends the results of Chen, Seeger, Srivastava and Technau on space curves, while providing a structural picture well-suited for generalisations. The re- sults and methods of this work precede the emergence of highly capable AI models.
item.dc:creator: Lauritz Streck

item.title: A $p$-adic Riemann--Hilbert correspondence over Robba rings
item.description: arXiv:2610.21065v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct overconvergent period sheaves $\mathcal{O}\widetilde{\mathbb{C}}^{I,\dagger}$ and $\mathcal{O}\mathbb{B}_{\mathrm{dR}}^{\dagger,+}$ on the $v$-site of a liftable semi-stable formal scheme $\mathfrak{X}_Z$. By establishing a decompletion theorem for small representations, we prove a $p$-adic Riemann-Hilbert correspondence relating small $\widetilde{\mathbb{C}}^I$-local systems (resp. $\mathbb{B}_{\mathrm{dR}}^+$-local systems) on the generic fiber $X_Z$ to small flat connections on the associated period ringed spaces. We further analyze the local Frobenius action and show that this correspondence is compatible with the Frobenius structure. As an application, we prove a comparison theorem between the cohomology of these period sheaves and the rigid cohomology of the special fiber, refining results of Le Bras and Colmez--Nizio{\l}.
item.dc:creator: Zekun Chen, Ruochuan Liu, Yupeng Wang, Jiahong Yu, Xinwen Zhu

item.title: A Simple Proof of I. Chowla's Theorem on Addition of Residue Classes
item.description: arXiv:2610.22427v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a brief, elementary proof of a striking theorem by I. Chowla on the addition of residue classes (1937) which generalizes the famous result of Cauchy and Davenport to residue classes modulo a composite.
item.dc:creator: Drew Duncan

item.title: Presentability of categories of localizations and analytic rings
item.description: arXiv:2610.22494v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that certain categories of Bousfield localizations are presentable and give explicit regular cardinals $\kappa$ for which they are $\kappa$-presentable. As an application, we show that the category of analytic rings in the sense of Clausen and Scholze is $(2^{\aleph_0})^+$-presentable.
item.dc:creator: Wern Juin Gabriel Ong, Gabriel Ribeiro

item.title: Rational Area Profiles of Regular Polygons Cut by Two Congruent Diagonals
item.description: arXiv:2610.22970v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Two congruent diagonals of a regular hexagon cut it into four regions whose areas are all rational multiples of the area of the hexagon. We determine when this phenomenon occurs in a regular $n$-gon. For every regular polygon cut by two intersecting congruent diagonals, neither of which is a diameter, we classify all unions of the four resulting regions whose areas are rational fractions of the total area. The hexagon is the only configuration in which all four regions are simultaneously rational. One of the two regions on the axis of symmetry is rational in exactly five sporadic configurations, with $n=6,18,30$, whereas the other region and the adjacent two-region unions belong to infinite families with simple geometric explanations. The two lateral regions have rational area ratios in exactly two configurations, with $n=6$ and $n=12$. The proof reduces each area ratio to a trigonometric quotient, bounds its rational values by norms in cyclotomic fields, and settles the remaining equations using Myerson's classification of equal products of two sines and the Poonen--Rubinstein classification of a three-sine-product equation.
item.dc:creator: Shoichi Inoue, Keiichi Watanabe

item.title: Whittaker Functionals for Exceptional Representations
item.description: arXiv:2610.23169v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In the study of automorphic forms on covering groups, Kazhdan-Patterson gives a formula that determines when the Whittaker functionals of induced representations can be descended to exceptional representations. In this paper, first, following the original approach given by Kazhdan-Patterson and applying the block-compatible 2-cocycle of Banks-Levy-Sepanski, we fill in several details omitted in the original proof. Secondly, we compare the formula of Kazhdan-Patterson with that of McNamara and Gao, which is formulated in a more general setting.
item.dc:creator: Sihan Li

item.title: Seven ordered points and the nonexistence of arithmetic ball quotient compactifications
item.description: arXiv:2610.23227v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the ordered GIT quotient of seven points on $\mathbb P^1$ with equal weights is not isomorphic to the Baily--Borel compactification of any arithmetic complex ball quotient. Together with our companion paper and the known positive examples, this determines the equal weight case for every $n\ge6$: such a realization exists precisely for $n=6,8$. The lattice and the algebraic isomorphism are unrestricted, and torsion and divisorial ramification are allowed. The proof combines arithmetic reductions with identities involving Chern classes of fixed subvarieties and intersection inequalities for nef divisors on the GIT quotient. The final comparison includes all fixed components and requires no bound on the degree of an individual fixed curve.
item.dc:creator: Ryunosuke Nakano (Hokkaido University), Hisato Matsukawa (Hokkaido University)

item.title: Weighted configurations and the nonexistence of arithmetic ball quotient compactifications
item.description: arXiv:2610.23228v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that, for every $n\ge9$, no ordered GIT quotient of $n$ points on $\mathbb P^1$ with positive rational weights smaller than one and of total weight two is isomorphic to the Baily--Borel compactification of an arithmetic complex ball quotient. The weights may lie on stability walls, and the lattice may have torsion and ramify along divisors. No compatibility with a prescribed period map is assumed. The proof compares homomorphisms from the tangent bundle to line bundles of negative degree with normal bundles of arithmetic fixed subvarieties. We describe these homomorphisms through coincident marked points and prove vanishing statements for their kernels. The comparison, together with integrality of Chern classes and the invariant theory of finite reflection groups, gives the nonexistence theorem without a Fano assumption on the GIT quotient.
item.dc:creator: Ryunosuke Nakano (Hokkaido University), Hisato Matsukawa (Hokkaido University)

item.title: Brauer-Manin obstruction for symmetric powers
item.description: arXiv:2610.23430v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a quasi-projective smooth geometrically integral variety $X$ over a number field, we prove that the Brauer-Manin obstruction for its symmetric powers coincides with the obstruction coming from $X$. As a consequence, Brauer-Manin obstruction for the symmetric powers cannot provide new cohomological obstruction to weak approximation of zero-cycles for $X$. The key intermediate ingredients are a Dold-Thom type result for Brauer groups and a precise descent formula for adelic points.
item.dc:creator: Yang Cao, Lin Zhou

item.title: On the asymptotic growth of the norm of the partial sum operator on $\mathscr H^1$
item.description: arXiv:2610.23666v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that the norm of the partial sum operator $S_N$ on the Hardy space $\mathscr H^1$ of Dirichlet series satisfies $$\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac{\log\log N}{\log N}\lVert S_N\rVert_{\mathscr H^1\to\mathscr H^1}\geq\frac{1-\log 2}{2\pi}.$$ Combined with an upper bound of Bondarenko, Brevig, Saksman and Seip, this shows that $$\lVert S_N\rVert_{\mathscr H^1\to\mathscr H^1}\asymp\frac{\log N}{\log\log N}$$ as $N\to\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Viktor Andersson

item.title: Correlations of values of random diagonal forms
item.description: arXiv:2211.02469v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the value distribution of diagonal forms in k variables and degree d with random real coefficients and positive integer variables, normalized so that mean spacing is one. We show that the l-correlation of almost all such forms is Poissonian when k is large enough depending on l and d.
item.dc:creator: Valentin Blomer, Junxian Li

item.title: A Database of Continued Fractions of Polynomial Type
item.description: arXiv:2409.06086v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We describe a database of 1925 continued fractions with polynomial coefficients, of which more than 1600 are new, both for interesting constants and for transcendental functions, and provide the database inside the \TeX\ source of the paper. Look in particular at the section ``Table of Contents''.
item.dc:creator: Henri Cohen

item.title: Galois measures and the Katz map
item.description: arXiv:2504.20558v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The purpose of this paper is to explain the proofs of the results announced by Nick Katz in 1977, namely a description of ``Galois measures for Tate modules of height two formal groups over the ring of integers of a finite unramified extension of $\mathbf{Q}_p$''.
item.dc:creator: Laurent Berger

item.title: On properness of moduli stacks of $D^{\times}$-shtukas over ramified legs
item.description: arXiv:2505.18977v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given a maximal order $\mathcal{D}$ of a central division algebra $D$ over a global function field $F$, we prove an explicit necessary and sufficient condition for moduli stacks of $\mathcal{D}^\times$-shtukas to be proper over a finite field (modulo a suitable central action) in terms of the local invariants of $D$ and bounds. Our result extends E. Lau's criterion (Duke Math. J. 140 (2007)) for properness of the leg morphism (or characteristic morphism) away from the ramification locus of $D$ to allow legs at ramified places. We also establish non-emptiness of Newton and Kottwitz-Rapoport strata for moduli stacks of $\mathcal{B}^\times$-shtukas, where $\mathcal{B}$ is a maximal order of a central simple algebra over $F$.
item.dc:creator: Yong-Gyu Choi, Wansu Kim, Junyeong Park

item.title: Rationality fields of CM modular forms
item.description: arXiv:2509.24119v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We formulate a conjecture on the finitude of rationality fields (i.e., Fourier coefficient fields) of newforms of bounded degree, and prove this for CM forms assuming a generalized Riemann hypothesis. Then we explicitly determine what quadratic and cubic rationality fields occur for weight 2 CM forms, which is related to classifications of CM abelian varieties of GL(2) type. Several of these fields do not appear in the existing tables of newforms in the LMFDB.
item.dc:creator: Kimball Martin

item.title: Bilinear forms with trace functions
item.description: arXiv:2511.09459v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We obtain non-trivial bounds for bilinear sums of trace functions below the P\'olya-Vinogradov range assuming only that the geometric monodromy group of the underlying ell-adic sheaf satisfies certain simple structural properties, in contrast to previous works which handled only special cases of Kloosterman and hypergeometric sheaves. Our approach builds on a general "soft" stratification theorem for sums of products of trace functions, based on an idea of Junyan Xu, combined with a new robust version of the Goursat-Kolchin-Ribet criterion.
item.dc:creator: \'Etienne Fouvry, Emmanuel Kowalski, Philippe Michel, Will Sawin

item.title: Cuspidal distinction via intertwining periods
item.description: arXiv:2512.19831v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Local intertwining periods have so far been used to reduce distinction of a general irreducible representation to distinction of cuspidal ones, for which other tools -- type theory, local and global trace formulae -- take over. The main contribution of this paper is to prove that they can be used to decide distinction of cuspidal representations themselves. We develop this approach with three well-studied examples for which the ambient group is an inner form of $\mathrm{GL}_n$ over a $p$-adic field, namely linear models, their non-split twisted version, and the quaternionic symplectic model. As consequences, we obtain proofs valid in arbitrary residual characteristic of the cuspidal case of the epsilon dichotomy conjecture of Prasad and Takloo-Bighash and of Prasad's conjecture on quaternionic symplectic models. The proof in the quaternionic symplectic model case, although going through intertwining periods, uses the simplest ones, namely closed intertwining periods, and is disappointingly short and elementary.
item.dc:creator: Nadir Matringe

item.title: On divisor sums due to Erd\H{o}s and Ramanujan
item.description: arXiv:2605.00695v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $d(n)$ denote the number of divisors of a positive integer $n$. A classical problem in analytic number theory is given by the asymptotic behavior of the divisor sum $\sum_{n \leq x} \frac{1}{d(n)}$, with Ramanujan having introduced an asymptotic formula for this sum with an explicit evaluation for the constant $A_1$ for the leading term $A_1 \frac{x}{\sqrt{\log x}}$. Gabdullin et al. recently considered a hybrid of this problem and the Titchmarsh divisor problem concerning $\sum_{p\leq x} d(p-1)$, proving that $\sum_{p\leq x} \frac{1}{d(p-1)} \asymp \frac{x}{(\log x)^{3/2}}$. This result and Erd\H{o}s's asymptotic formula $ \sum_{n \leq x} d(d(n)) \sim c_1 \, x \log \log x $ for a constant $c_1 \in (0, \infty)$ lead us to consider the hybrid $\sum_{n \leq x} \frac{1}{d(d(n))}$ of the Erd\H{o}s and Ramanujan divisor sums. In this paper, we prove that there exists a constant $c_3 \in (0, \infty)$ such that $$\sum_{n \leq x} \frac{1}{d(d(n))} \sim c_3 \frac{x}{ \log \log x}, $$ through a combined application of Golomb's estimate for powerful numbers, Tur\'{a}n's quantitative form of the Hardy-Ramanujan theorem, and a fourth-moment estimate for the number of distinct prime divisors due to Granville and Soundararajan. Moreover, an explicit formula for the constant $c_3$ is given.
item.dc:creator: John M. Campbell

item.title: On $\mathbb{Z}_2$-extensions of real quadratic fields
item.description: arXiv:2606.00482v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $k$ be a real quadratic field. Let $k_n$ be the $n$-th layer of the $\mathbb{Z}_2$-extension of $k$, and $2^{a_n}$ be the $2$-part of the class number of $k_n$. In this paper, we derive many laws concerning the sequence $(a_0,a_1,\dotsc)$, by iteratively extending the group of cyclotomic units.
item.dc:creator: Sosuke Sasaki

item.title: Continued Fractions of Polynomial Type: Theory and Encyclopedic Dictionary
item.description: arXiv:2607.06581v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: After giving a number of properties of continued fractions of polynomial type, in particular focusing on convergence properties and Bauer-Muir-Ap\'ery acceleration techniques, we give a large list of continued fractions, both for specific real numbers, and for special functions, some extracted from a number of different sources, but most others being probably new. In addition to providing such a list, one of our main additions is to include the exact speed of convergence of these continued fractions (sometimes only up to a multiplicative constant), which is almost always omitted in the literature.
item.dc:creator: Henri Cohen

item.title: On the Squarefree Values of Degree-$2q$ Polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2608.10335v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we show that if $h(x)$ is an irreducible monic integer polynomial of degree $2q$ (with $q$ prime), whose defining field extension of $\mathbb{Q}$ contains a Galois extension of degree $q$, then there is a positive density of integers $n$ such that $h(n)$ is squarefree; in particular, $h(n)$ is squarefree for infinitely many integers $n$. As an application, we prove that the family of exceptional cubic fields contains an infinite subfamily whose unit shapes converge to the hexagonal lattice. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first example of a family of non-Galois totally real cubic fields whose unit shapes converge to the hexagonal lattice.
item.dc:creator: Sergio Ricardo Zapata Ceballos, Fatemeh Jalalvand

item.title: The arithmetic of critical values II: critical elliptic curves
item.description: arXiv:2608.29836v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this second chapter of the $\textit{Arithmetic of critical values}$ series (ACV), we study certain double covers $E_f\to\mathbb{P}^1$ whose branch locus coincides with that of a quartic polynomial $f$. We give a direct proof of the fact, already shown non-constructively in ACV I, that the elliptic curves $E_f$ admit a $3$-isogeny. Our methods are Galois-theoretic, and lead us to a thorough analysis of the Galois closure of $f:\mathbb{P}^1\to\mathbb{P}^1$. We exploit its rich geometry to prove a Selmer companionship theorem for the family $E_f$, allowing us to exhibit elements in certain Tate-Shafarevich groups which are visible in an abelian surface. We also give some dynamical and Diophantine applications of our constructions, as well as new examples of Jacobians isogenous to a power of an elliptic curve.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Naccarato

item.title: Universal norms and de Rham representations
item.description: arXiv:2609.09862v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The purpose of this note is to show that the computation of the universal norms in Iwasawa cohomology for the $p$-adic cyclotomic extension implies an analogous result for any $p$-adic extension that contains the cyclotomic extension. In addition, we prove a twisted cyclotomic variant, which applies to all Lubin--Tate extensions.
item.dc:creator: Laurent Berger

item.title: Solutions of $x_1^2+x_2^2-x_3^2=D$ with small $x_3$: a spectral approach
item.description: arXiv:2610.15706v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We count the integral solutions of $x_1^2+x_2^2-x_3^2=D$ weighted by $\Phi(x_3/M)$, for $M$ smaller than $\sqrt D$. Such solutions correspond to binary quadratic forms of discriminant $D$, and the count becomes a sum, over the geodesics of discriminant $D$, of a function of their distance to the point $i$. We evaluate it by the spectral theory of automorphic forms. Throughout, $\theta=7/64$. For square $D=n^2$ the geodesics run from cusp to cusp, and Hecke theory reduces them to the single geodesic from $0$ to $\infty$. For every $n$ and both parities of $x_3$, we obtain an asymptotic formula with error $O(n^{1+\theta+\varepsilon}M^{-1/2})$, using the Kim-Sarnak bound and the large sieve of Deshouillers and Iwaniec (and the theta group for the parity of $x_3$). It is non-trivial for $M\ge n^{71/96+\varepsilon}$. This improves the range $n^{5/6+\varepsilon}$ of the elementary method, and confirms the corrected main term of the author's earlier work. For non-square $D=f^2D_0$ the geodesics are closed. A Hecke relation for their traces reduces everything to the fundamental discriminant $D_0$. We obtain an error $O(D^{\varepsilon}f^{1+\theta}D_0^{2/3}M^{-1/2})$, using the formulas of Duke-Imamoglu-Toth and Baruch-Mao together with the cubic moment bound of Young and of Andersen-Wu. For $D\equiv 5 \bmod 8$ this counts all solutions, and the range $M\ge D^{1/2-1/1332}$ of Friedlander and Iwaniec improves to $M\ge D^{4/9+\varepsilon}$. This paper was written in collaboration with Claude (Opus 5.5, High), an AI model developed by Anthropic.
item.dc:creator: Stephan Baier

item.title: A matching lower bound for the sextic large sieve and structured prime moments
item.description: arXiv:2610.17675v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the contrast between the large-sieve norm and the second moment of structured prime coefficients for sextic residue characters over the Eisenstein integers. For squarefree row and column ideals of norms at most A and B, we prove a lower bound of order (AB)^(-epsilon) times (A + B + A^(5/6) B^(1/3) + A^(1/3) B^(5/6)), matching de Faveri's upper bound throughout the full parameter range. In particular, the squared full-cutoff norm at balance is at least Q^(7/6 - epsilon). The proof uses the uniform unmarked character moments of OpenAI's September 2026 manuscript, a Gauss second moment uniform in moving prime exclusions, and a centered comparison that transports a squarefree-row signal between column scales. With the additional unmarked inverse moment and buffered zero detector from the same source, we derive a low-height zero-density estimate and bound the second moment of a fixed smooth prime sum by Q^((37 - 10 sqrt(6))/6 + epsilon). We also treat bounded convolutions of independently weighted large primes. An appendix retains the first version's unbalanced lower bound and its exponent 17/16, without using the additional plain or inverse moment estimates.
item.dc:creator: Yuanda Xu, Hejian Sang

item.title: Enumerating Integral Points on Triangles in $\mathbb{R}^3$
item.description: arXiv:2610.20899v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present two ways of constructing Ehrhart polynomials corresponding to certain triangles in $\mathbb{R}^3$. One of our methods employs Popoviciu's Theorem, while the other method uses a version of Pick's Theorem adapted to rank-2 lattices in $\mathbb{R}^3$. We then apply our methods to linear Diophantine equations of the form $ax+by+cz=n$ and develop upper and lower bounds on the number of solutions in nonnegative integers $x$, $y$, and $z$. The bounds we develop are closed form quasi-polynomials, and the difference between them is bounded by a constant depending only on $a$ and $b$. As an application, we prove that the $k$th Frobenius number exists for any triple of positive integers and any $k$.
item.dc:creator: Max Aldrich, Daniel Gulbrandsen, Clara Keddy

item.title: An introduction to algebraic groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.21926v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We review the theory of abelian varieties and, more generally, algebraic groups, with a view toward arithmetic applications. We discuss their models over the rings of integers of number fields, their reductions modulo primes, their torsion points (together with their natural Galois action), and the interplay of these notions through characteristic polynomials of Frobenius.
item.dc:creator: Davide Lombardo

item.title: Toric schemes and integral models for Shimura varieties with $\Gamma_1(p)$-type level
item.description: arXiv:2602.23245v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose a conjectural theory of $p$-integral models of Shimura varieties with level structure at $p$ given by a class of normal subgroups of parahoric subgroups with abelian quotient group. The role of the theory of local models is played in this context by a certain root stack over the local model for parahoric level. The construction of this root stack is based on the "divisor theorem" (a foundational fact about local models) and on the theory of toric varieties in this context, both of which are of independent interest. We prove our conjecture in the case of Shimura varieties of PEL type when the parahoric is an Iwahori (under some additional conditions).
item.dc:creator: Georgios Pappas, Michael Rapoport

item.title: Modular Constructions of g-Golomb Rulers
item.description: arXiv:2607.07931v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A set \(\mathcal{G}\) of integers is a \(g\)-Golomb ruler if each positive difference appears at most \(g\) times between any 2 elements of the set, and \(G(g,n)\) denotes the minimum diameter of such a ruler with \(n\) marks. We prove a general lemma for passing from certain modular constructions to ordinary \(g\)-Golomb rulers. The key point is that, in a modular \(g\)-Golomb ruler, no cyclic gap length can occur more than \(g\) times. This gives a larger guaranteed cut than the previous average gap argument. We apply this lemma to cyclic relative difference sets, Singer sets, Ruzsa--Spence rulers, and Paley quadratic residues to provide many competing constructions for \(g\)-Golomb Rulers. A computation on the grid \(1\le g\le500\), \(n=g+b\), \(2\le b\le500\), compares the four resulting construction families.
item.dc:creator: Aditya Gupta

item.title: Counterexamples to the Minimum Period Conjecture for Restricted Partition Functions
item.description: arXiv:2608.02085v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a finite sequence of positive integers $\boldsymbol{a}=(a_1,\dots,a_n)$, the restricted partition function $q_{\boldsymbol{a}}(k)$ denote the number of nonnegative integer solutions to the equation $a_1x_1+a_2x_2+\cdots +a_nx_n=k$. It is proved to be a quasi-polynomial of degree $n-1$. Write $q_{\boldsymbol{a}}(k)=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}c_j(k)k^j$ with periodic coefficient functions $c_j$, and set $b_m=\#\{i:m\mid a_i\}$. In 2008, Beck, Sam, and Woods conjectured that the minimum period of $c_j(k)$ is $\mathrm{lcm}\{m:b_m>j\}$. In this paper, we derive an exact root-of-unity formula for every coefficient function $c_j(k)$. The formula proves the conjectured divisibility upper bound, but it also reveals a lower bound for the period of $c_j(k)$. Both divisibility bounds are sharp. This leads us to construct a family of counterexamples to this conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Feihu Liu, Jinlong Tang, Guoce Xin, Chen Zhang

item.title: Hankel Transform and $(\alpha,\beta)$ Somos-4 Sequences
item.description: arXiv:2608.08703v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: An $(\alpha,\beta)$ Somos-$4$ sequence $S_n$ is defined by the recurrence $S_nS_{n-4}=\alpha S_{n-1}S_{n-3}+\beta S_{n-2}^2$ ($n\geq 4$), with suitable initial values, where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are constant parameters. A widely studied question is the following: When does the Hankel transform of a generating function become an $(\alpha,\beta)$ Somos-4 sequence? In particular, how can $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be derived for such a function? A sufficient condition for this problem has been established by Wang and Zhang. In this paper, we obtain the following three main results. (i): We extend the Wang--Zhang sufficient condition by working over the rational function field. Then we combine this result with the Sulanke--Xin quadratic transformation to resolve all of Barry's currently unsolved $(\alpha,\beta)$ Somos-4 conjectures, which arise in diverse contexts, including generalized Catalan recurrences, Riordan arrays, generalized Bernstein arrays, and elliptic curves. (ii): We show that the odd and even subsequences of an $(\alpha,\beta)$ Somos-4 sequence are again $(\alpha,\beta)$ Somos-4 sequences with transformed parameters. This is employed to establish Barry's Hurwitz transform conjecture. (iii): Using the theory of orthogonal polynomials, we prove a Hankel determinant formula and thereby prove a conjecture related to the $(\alpha,\beta)$ Somos-4 sequence. In addition, we prove some conjectures on formulas for periodic Hankel determinants.
item.dc:creator: Feihu Liu, Ying Wang, Zihao Zhang
